item.title: Playground
item.description:
https://go-wasmcontainers.github.io/playground/ is a terminal in a web page running wctr against WASI containers. There is no server: the engine runs in the page (the browser executor, runtime/browser, new in engine v0.2.0). The playground’s latest release is v0.1.0; the page since gained the completion and line editing below, which come from engine v0.3.0.

Completion and editing

The terminal completes with Tab, as a shell does: subcommands, flags, -m sizes, local images (for run and rmi), the catalogue of images to pull, container names and IDs (logs, rm, inspect, and only running containers for kill) and image arguments. Editing is bash-style: Up and Down for the history, Ctrl-R to search it, Ctrl-A, Ctrl-E, Ctrl-B and Ctrl-F to move, Ctrl-U, Ctrl-K and Ctrl-W to cut, Ctrl-D, and Ctrl-L to clear. The history is kept per tab (in sessionStorage). From a keypress to the line on screen took 7 to 14 ms in Chromium and 23 ms in Firefox, measured in CI.

The line editor and its completion are the package cli/lineedit of the engine: pure Go, usable by anyone who embeds the engine’s CLI.

What you can type

wctr pull, run, ps, logs, rm, rmi, images, inspect and kill, plus help and clear. run takes --rm, -d, --name, -e, -w, -m and --entrypoint. Exit codes are the native engine’s: the container’s own, or 125, 126, 127, 134 and 137; see Commands.

$ wctr run --rm hello
$ wctr run --rm -e NAME=you greet

Images

Image What it is
hello, greet the small demonstration modules
lab a module with subcommands: echo, env, pwd, ls, cat, write, count, sleep, spin, hog, bench, fs, exit, esc
age:1.3.2, go-md2man:2.0.7, shfmt:3.14.1 pkgx wasip1 bottles

go-pkgx now also builds C tools for wasip1 (lua 5.4.9, sqlite 3.53.4, zlib 1.3.2 with minigzip). They are planned for this catalogue with engine v0.9.0 and are not live yet.

Images and pulls survive a reload: they are kept in the browser’s IndexedDB. So do the containers (engine v0.4.0): state, exit code, logs and written files. A container that was running comes back exited with code 137, and a --rm one is removed.

Offline and updates

The playground works offline. A new version installs in the background and applies when you choose “Reload to update”. Only one tab runs the engine at a time; another tab can take over with “Use it here”. The engine was ready in 130–190 ms on a first visit in Chromium, 80–115 ms after a reload, and 75 ms offline.

Limits per container

256 MiB of memory, a 5-minute run, 64 MiB of writes, 4 MiB of logs, and 64 containers at once.

Not yet

No stdin, no shell, no networking. Ctrl-C stops waiting for a container but leaves it running. See Limitations and the roadmap.

Speed

Measured in one CI run, the page is ready in 0.46 s in Chromium and 1.0 s in Firefox, and the first hello runs in 81 ms and 291 ms. Cold start is slower than wasmtime (23 ms natively). The table is on Performance.
